artists.biography:
Kamasi Washington was born in Los Angeles, California, on February 2, 1981 to musical parents and educators, and was raised in Inglewood, California. He is a graduate of the Academy of Music of Alexander Hamilton High School in Beverlywood, Los Angeles. Washington next enrolled in UCLA's Department of Ethnomusicology, where he began playing with faculty members such as Kenny Burrell, Billy Higgins and band leader/trumpeter Gerald Wilson. Washington features in the album Young Jazz Giants in 2004. He has played along with a diverse group of musicians including Wayne Shorter, Herbie Hancock, Horace Tapscott, Gerald Wilson, Lauryn Hill, Nas, Snoop Dogg, George Duke, Chaka Khan, Flying Lotus, Thundercat, Mike Muir, Francisco Aguabella, the Pan Afrikaan People's Orchestra and Raphael Saadiq.

Washington ventured into big band music when he joined the Gerald Wilson Orchestra for their 2006 album In My Time. Washington played saxophone on Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp a Butterfly. His debut solo recording, The Epic, was released in May 2015 to critical acclaim. His second studio album, Heaven and Earth, was released in June 2018, with a companion EP titled The Choice released a week later.

perplexity.description:
Fearless Movement is Kamasi Washington's fifth studio album, released in May 2024 on the Young label. Spanning nearly ninety minutes, the album represents a deliberate creative pivot toward what Washington describes as his "dance album"—though he clarifies the concept as metaphorical, equating dance with "movement and expression" and the practice of spiritual flexibility through music. The sonic palette draws from jazz-funk, modern jazz, modal music, spiritual jazz, fusion, and post-bop traditions, grounded in an earthly, embodied aesthetic that reflects Washington's recent experience with fatherhood.

The album showcases Washington's collaborative approach, featuring core members of his West Coast Get Down collective including Thundercat, Brandon Coleman, Terrace Martin, and Patrice Quinn, alongside guest appearances from André 3000, George Clinton, D Smoke, BJ the Chicago Kid, and DJ Battlecat. The ensemble arrangements emphasize collective composition, with several band members receiving writing credits alongside Washington. Cameron Graves contributes piano across most tracks, while Coleman's keyboards and organ work provide harmonic depth throughout the record's extended instrumental passages.

Within Washington's discography, Fearless Movement marks a shift in thematic focus from his previous work, prioritizing accessibility and rhythmic vitality while maintaining the saxophonist's sophisticated harmonic language and spiritual underpinnings. The album's emphasis on elasticity and possibility—both musical and existential—positions it as a statement on artistic renewal and the importance of sustained creative risk-taking, themes that have defined Washington's career since his breakthrough work in the 2010s.
